best.hypothesis: Normalize and merge the input monomials, construct one shared monomial Gram map, and lift its coefficients through an exact sparse change of coordinates. This may reduce repeated CAR work when operators share monomials; no measured improvement is claimed.
best.mechanism: Adjacent CAR rewrites first produce exact canonical operator coefficients. A reverse incidence list records which operators contain each surviving monomial. The monomial Gram map is then transformed using cached integer coordinate weights. A diagonal monomial coordinate contributes a_i^2 on operator diagonals and 2*a_i*a_j off diagonal. An off-diagonal monomial coordinate contributes a_i*b_i on diagonals and a_i*b_j+b_i*a_j off diagonal. All cancellations use Python integers.
best.assumptions: The supplied monomial_map obeys its exact symmetric Gram contract and stores its backend caches in payload['cache']. Input coefficients are Python integers, flags are 0/1, modes are nonnegative integers, and all nonzero input monomials share one charge. Canonicalization preserves that charge. Empty operators and linear dependencies require no special assumptions.
best.failure_cases: Dense incidence lists can make the cached coordinate transfers large. Dictionaries with little monomial reuse may not offset normalization and transformation overhead. Output size can remain quadratic in the number of operators. Mixed charges and noninteger coefficients are outside the specified domain. Runtime and correctness have not been experimentally checked here.
